title: Sign in (app request)
summary: The first step of the hosted sign-in card when DJDL on a Mac asks someone to sign in: identifier first (the browser offers saved passkeys from the same field), then DJDL's own store account (a product connection) and the built-in providers DJDL ships with. Email and passkeys are always on; there are no per-product sign-in switches behind this card.
compare: The card keeps SIGN-IN.md §3.1's measures: 456 px wide, 22 px radius, 48 px fields and buttons, 52 px provider buttons, the lockup at 18 px in muted text above it (an app context), and Help · Privacy · Terms under it. No 'Polaris Key · key.plrs.im' line.

The app header reads 'DJDL wants you to sign in' with the 56 px DJDL icon, then 'Example Audio · on Studio Mac mini' with a desktop icon (the icon follows the device kind: desktop, laptop or phone). Name and icon come from Core's Presentation (HA-12), not a per-product 'App name' field.

The email field is the first and only primary path: one Continue. The address decides what happens next (see identity.sign-in-routes); there is no 'Continue with single sign-on' button for platform connections.

The email field carries autocomplete="username webauthn", so the browser offers a saved passkey as the person types (conditional UI) and choosing it signs in with no code. That suggestion is the browser's own chrome: it isn't drawn here and won't appear in built screenshots.

DJDL's product connection shows as one labelled, full-width button ('Continue with your DJDL store account', with DJDL's icon) above the logo-only row, and only on DJDL's card (I-32). A product connection that is token-exchange only (Diceroll accounts) never shows a button.

The provider row follows where DJDL ships: Apple (macOS) and Google, two equal halves, logo only, accessible names 'Continue with Apple' and 'Continue with Google'. Steam is absent because DJDL isn't on Steam. Google's G keeps its four colors.
'Sign in with a passkey' is a ghost button under the row; 'Have a license key?' and 'Sign in with another device' are quiet links under a rule, each with a 44 px target.
The footer says 'Polaris Key signs you in for DJDL. Example Audio never sees your codes or passkeys.' with a lock, and stays on every step of this sign-in.

Nothing on the card depends on a product toggle for email or passkeys (I-29 retires oidc_enabled, magic_enabled, license_key_claim_enabled and auto_link_enabled). The only way they disappear is an organization requiring SSO for the typed address's domain.
Phone: the card goes edge to edge under a 56 px lockup row, the star field is dropped, the two quiet links stack as full-width 44 px rows, and every target stays at least 44 px.

designReview.reviewer: UX designer (visual critique of rendered screenshots)
designReview.verdict: Pass. The quiet links have 44 px targets and the device icon follows the device kind.

findings.issue: On phone the quiet links were about 20 px tall against the 44 px promise; a laptop icon stood for a Mac mini.
findings.resolution: The links are 44 px tall at every width and stack as full-width rows on phone. The device line uses the desktop (monitor) icon here, on sign-in-routes and wherever Studio Mac mini appears.
